_: Hand-labelled strike times for the long raw takes in fixtures/raw/ — the first ground truth
this project has for anything. Read it with scripts/checkaudio.py --truth.
video_impact_sec is the PICTURE: the last frame with the ball still on the mat, read off a
frame-accurate strip (scripts/checkstrip.py) where the frame before it has the ball and the
frame after it does not. At ~59 fps the label is therefore good to about +/-0.017 s, and no
better — do not quote it more precisely than that.
audio_onset_sec is the SOUND: the first 5 ms window whose >4 kHz energy crosses four times
its local median floor. This is the earliest instant a detector working on audio alone could
possibly report, so it is what detector error is measured against.
The gap between the two columns is 0.121-0.148 s across five takes shot at three different
ball speeds. It does not scale with ball speed, so it is recording-pipeline latency (audio
timestamps lagging video), not the flight time of the ball to the screen. IT IS A PROPERTY OF
THESE FILES, which the stock Samsung camera app recorded — SwingSage's own MediaRecorder path
is a different pipeline and has never been measured. Do not compensate for it in the product
